The actor's plan to automate attempts against customer loyalty accounts and gift-card balances was executed through a series of coordinated technical manipulations. The specific step involved implementing sequential sign-in attempts against the customer authentication endpoint using robotized HTTP requests with shifted date-time headers. This approach allowed the actor to systematically test account credentials without triggering immediate security alerts.

The actor exploited the misconfigured session token refresh flow by submitting expired credentials into the validation endpoint, effectively hijacking active sessions. This method leveraged a known vulnerability in the token validation process to gain unauthorized access to multiple accounts simultaneously.

The actor generated random login identifiers and passwords via scripted bulk account forge tools to imitate legitimate user activity. This technique created the appearance of normal shopping behavior while actually compromising account security and accessing sensitive financial data.

The actor purchased low-value gift cards and immediately traded them for high-demand consumable goods and cash equivalents to obscure the origin of funds. This rapid conversion strategy made it difficult for fraud detection systems to trace the money back to the compromised loyalty accounts.

The actor recorded all transaction details in encrypted local files and employed fake billing addresses and device fingerprints to bypass fraud detection. This comprehensive obfuscation approach created a layered defense against security investigations while maintaining plausible deniability of the fraudulent activities.
